basis: Leishmania infection directly causes cutaneous nodules and ulcers; mucosal or visceral disease is not intrinsic to this concept.
Elevated intraocular pressure causes glaucomatous optic nerve damage; the optic nerve is included in the ocular axis.
Estrogen synthesis deficiency; osteopenia, osteoporosis and delayed skeletal maturation occur in 80-99%. Associated fatty liver is a separate metabolic liver diagnosis.
Retinal vascular development and vitreoretinal disease define the spectrum; osteoporosis affects particular subtypes and is not established in most across the umbrella.
Inherited inflammatory bowel disease causes immune-mediated intestinal inflammation; no common direct extraintestinal damage is established here.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; myopia/astigmatism, chronic bowel dysfunction and foot deformities occur in 80-99%. Central breathing dysregulation does not establish lung damage.
Hereditary cutaneous hyperpigmentation and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis; no extracutaneous organ damage is described.
Congenital facial palsy and impaired ocular abduction define it; clubfoot/pectoral hypoplasia occur in 30-79%, dental abnormalities in 37%. Hearing loss is occasional.
Hereditary congenital facial nerve dysfunction; hearing impairment is variable and its frequency is not established at 30%.
Defined by reflux into the stomach, esophagus or pancreas; bile content and biliary ancestry do not establish liver or bile duct injury.
Microcephalic developmental and skeletal disorder; central hypothyroidism in 2/2 and subglottic stenosis in 30-79%. Microtia in 2/2 omitted under the four-axis cap.
Infection-associated inflammation of fetal membranes; the anatomical site has no axis, but the bacterial infection mechanism does.
Protozoal infection; CNS dysfunction occurs in 80-99%, anemia commonly (~30%+). Major cardiac injury is not established at 30%; renal and endocrine dysfunction are occasional.
Cardiac electrical disorder defined by early repolarization associated with ventricular fibrillation.
Primary lung adenocarcinoma with Clara cell or type II pneumocyte differentiation; no extra-pulmonary involvement is intrinsic.
Neurodevelopmental and cutaneous manifestations span major subtypes. Cardiac and skeletal lesions vary substantially; no common damaging manifestation is established across the umbrella.
Defined by autoimmune injury to hepatocytes and red blood cells, producing giant cell hepatitis and autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
Delirium is a disorder of cerebral attention, awareness and cognition, explicitly included in the neurologic axis.
Inhalation can cause direct airway injury; ingestion causes corrosive gastrointestinal injury. Route-dependent systemic complications lack a common frequency; transient irritation excluded.
Tumor arises in the vulva, a reproductive site outside the axes; rhabdomyoblastic differentiation does not establish a skeletal muscle primary.
Inherited glomerular disease with steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome in 6/6, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and progressive kidney failure.
Spectrum principally includes congenital brain abnormalities and developmental impairment with polydactyly or skeletal dysplasia; renal involvement cannot be inferred from ciliopathy alone.
Pulmonary hemosiderosis directly affects the lungs; associated gamma-A globulin deficiency denotes IgA immunodeficiency. Additional organ damage is not established.
A neurodevelopmental language acquisition disorder; no structural oral, hearing or other organ disease is required.
Defined by mitochondrial myopathy, lactic acidosis and sideroblastic anemia, establishing skeletal muscle, metabolic and blood involvement.
